messages.subject: Differential PTM level analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone.

MSstats make it easy to perform analyses of differential protein abundances.

Would a kind soul share an example of how to modify the conventional use of MSstats to analyse phospho-enriched samples?

I understand that it is possible because it has been conceptually mentioned before.

I am hoping to see one example and I will be very grateful.

Thank you.

Ivan

messages.subject: Re: Differential PTM level analysis
messages.body_plain:
The primary thing that you need is instead of having a column with protein ID, it needs to be a protein ID with a phosphorylation site, this way the sites are kept separate, instead of being grouped as a protein.  We use artMS r-package, which can take MaxQuant output, convert to a site based input file for MSstats, and then run MSstats.  http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/artMS.html

-Danielle

When running the following function

goldstandard.proposed_wo_outlier <- dataProcess(Test,
                                    normalization='equalizeMedians',
                                    summaryMethod="TMP",

                                    censoredInt="NA",

                                    featureSubset="highQuality",
                                    remove_uninformative_feature_outlier=TRUE)

1.

Joining, by = "protein"
Identifying low-coverage features...

Error: Problem with `mutate()` input `var_resid_eb`.
x Input `var_resid_eb` can't be recycled to size 1.
i Input `var_resid_eb` is `eb_fit$var.post <http://var.post>`.
i Input `var_resid_eb` must be size 1, not 3070.
i The error occured in group 1: protein = "A0A0C4DH29".

Do you have any idea why i get those two different errors and how i could overcome them?

Thank you very much for any help
Best regards
Matthias

messages.subject: Error during OpenSWATHtoMSstatsFormat
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSStats-Team,

I tried to analyze some DIA data which was anaylzed using OpenSwathWorkflow and exported using pyprophet using MSStats.

Following the instructions I tried to convert the OSW output to MSStats format using the OpenSWATHtoMSstatsFormat functionality.

However, i ended up getting this error:

> quant <- OpenSWATHtoMSstatsFormat(data_me,
+                                   annotation = annot,
+                                   filter_with_mscore = TRUE, ## same as default
+                                   mscore_cutoff = 0.01, ## same as default
+                                   removeProtein_with1Feature = TRUE)
** Remove the decoys.
** Features with great than 0.01 in m_score are removed.
Error: Assigned data `0` must be compatible with existing data.
i Error occurred for column `Intensity`.
x Can't convert <double> to <character>.
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
> rlang::last_error()
<error/tibble_error_assign_incompatible_type>
Assigned data `0` must be compatible with existing data.
i Error occurred for column `Intensity`.
x Can't convert <double> to <character>.
Backtrace:
 1. MSstats::OpenSWATHtoMSstatsFormat(...)
 3. tibble:::`[<-.tbl_df`(...)
 4. tibble:::tbl_subassign(x, i, j, value, i_arg, j_arg, substitute(value))
 5. tibble:::tbl_subassign_row(xj, i, value, value_arg)
 6. base::tryCatch(...)
 7. base:::tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
 8. base:::tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
 9. value[[3L]](cond)

Do you have any idea what could be the reason and how i could overcome this error?

Best regards and many thanks in advance for any help in this matter
Matthias
